        **Abstract**: In recent years, Graph Neural Network (GNN) based models have shown promis-
ing results in simulating physics of complex systems. However, training dedicated
graph network based physics simulators can be costly, as most models are confined
to fully supervised training, which requires extensive data generated from tradi-
tional physics simulators. To date, how transfer learning could improve the model
performance and training efficiency has remained unexplored. In this work, we
introduce a pre-training and transfer learning paradigm for graph network simula-
tors. We propose the scalable graph U-net (SGUNET). Incorporating an innovative
depth-first search (DFS) pooling, the SGUNET is adaptable to different mesh sizes
and resolutions for various simulation tasks. To enable the transfer learning be-
tween differently configured SGUNETs, we propose a set of mapping functions to
align the parameters between the pre-trained model and the target model. An extra
normalization term is also added into the loss to constrain the difference between
the pre-trained weights and target model weights for better generalization per-
formance. To pre-train our physics simulator we created a dataset which includes
20,000 physical simulations of randomly selected 3D shapes from the open source
A Big CAD (ABC) dataset. We show that our proposed transfer learning meth-
ods allow the model to perform even better when fine-tuned with small amounts
of training data than when it is trained from scratch with full extensive dataset.
On the 2D Deformable Plate benchmark dataset, our pre-trained model fine-tuned
on 1/16 of the training data achieved an 11.05% improvement in position RMSE
compared to the model trained from scratch.

#### **1. Core Innovation**  
The paper introduces a transfer learning framework for Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to improve the scalability and performance of physics simulators. ---

#### **2. Technical Approach**  
- **Scalable Graph U-Net (SGUNET)**: A GNN architecture designed to handle varying mesh sizes and resolutions for different simulation tasks.  
- **DFS Pooling**: An innovative pooling mechanism incorporated into SGUNET for effective feature extraction.  
- **Parameter Alignment Mapping Functions**: Custom functions developed to align the parameters between pre-trained and target models, facilitating knowledge transfer.  
- **Normalization Term in Loss Function**: An additional regularization term added to constrain the difference between pre-trained and target model weights, enhancing generalization.  
- **Training Dataset**: A dataset comprising 20,000 physical simulations of 3D shapes from the ABC dataset, used for pre-training the model.

#### **4. Limitations & Assumptions**  
- The study focuses on 3D simulations but tested the model on 2D tasks, which may limit its applicability to real-world scenarios requiring 3D modeling.  
- The effectiveness of transfer learning depends on the similarity between the source (pre-trained) and target (fine-tuned) tasks.  
- The dataset used for pre-training is specific to the ABC dataset, which may limit the generalizability of the approach to other datasets.  

---

#### **5. Domain Impact (Theoretical/Practical)**  
- **Theoretical**: The work provides a novel approach to leveraging transfer learning in GNNs for physics simulation, offering insights into the scalability and generalization capabilities of deep learning models in this domain.  
- **Practical**: The proposed framework reduces the computational and data requirements for training physics simulators, making it more accessible for applications where resources are constrained. This could lead to more efficient and scalable simulators for various physical systems.
